assessments.summary: Measles is peaking in the US with a 100% increase in reported cases compared to the same period last year, driven by a significant rise in weekly cases.
Dengue is peaking in the US with a 853% increase in reported cases compared to the same period last year, indicating a sharp rise in activity.
Mpox is peaking in the US with an 87% increase in reported cases compared to the same period last year, though cases have decreased from the previous year.
Influenza is rising globally with a 29% increase in test positivity compared to the previous month, and US hospital admissions have risen 58% over the past month.
Polio has rising interest in the US, with Wikipedia readership at the 97th percentile of the past year.
West Nile virus is rising in the US with a 1388% increase in reported cases compared to the same period last year, though cases have decreased from the previous year.
Group A strep has rising interest in the US, with Wikipedia readership at the 56th percentile of the past year.
Hepatitis A is at baseline in the US with a 10% increase in reported cases compared to the same period last year, though cases have decreased from the previous year.
Chikungunya cases in the US are stable at baseline with 7 weekly reports, while Switzerland reports its first locally acquired cases.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with 249 weekly reports, up 45% from the previous 8 months.
US hospital admissions for COVID-19 are stable at baseline with 4,519 weekly cases, up 5% from the previous month.
Global RSV test positivity is rising at 2.8% weekly, up 82% from the previous month, with US hospitalizations also increasing.
Whooping cough cases in the US are rising with 389 weekly reports, up 55% from the previous 8 months.
Malaria cases in the US are stable at baseline with 34 weekly reports, up 30% from the previous 8 months.
Typhoid fever Wikipedia readership is stable at the 43rd percentile of the past year.
